01-feature-building.notes: All 25 pass the 5 hidden contract tests and their own suites, so differentiation comes from my probes. P is the only real contract break: duplicate depends_on entries produce duplicate output, a bogus empty cycle error, or a masked cycle. D, H, L and X use recursive cycle diagnostics that raise RecursionError for blocked components of 1000 or more jobs. 02-bug-fixing.notes: All implementations except F and P pass the hidden contract tests and my 23-case probe harness; F and P keep expired entries after get, so behavioural scores are nearly flat and regression coverage decides most of the ranking. Regression coverage was measured with 20 mutants of a reference fix, run with both a purging and a non-purging __len__. The most common gap: purge-before-capacity is only observable when the expired entry is NOT the LRU entry (e.g. after a get refreshes it), and roughly half the suites test only the LRU-expired case, which plain LRU eviction already satisfies. Likewise eviction-on-update only shows up when the updated key is not the LRU key. Suites J and Q (and O, the other way round) assert __len__ semantics the spec does not define; they kill every mutant but reject many correct implementations, so they were docked to 1.5 (O to 1.0). Close calls: A vs I/K (all 9.75; ordered by mutant survivors and breadth), and the 8.75 cluster (B, O, P, R, S, U, W, Y), where P has the strongest tests but a contract miss, and Y's fabricated test output cost diagnosis. G/J purge only when the cache is full; I treated that as compliant with 'before enforcing capacity'. Not verified: behaviour under a clock that advances on every call. Several implementations call clock() more than once per put, which I judged immaterial.

05-technical-writing.notes: Closest call: S vs L, both 9.25. S ranks first for its safer freshness guidance (log the age, do not reject) and its retry-outcome table; L is equally strong on idempotency and open items. The 8.75 group (C, A, R, J) is ordered by breadth of flagged uncertainty; A and R are nearly identical in content and code. Cross-cutting: most single-secret Python examples raise TypeError in hmac.compare_digest on a non-ASCII signature header, which is minor robustness and was not penalised heavily. Examples that hard-code a 5-minute freshness window without the retry/replay caveat (D, F, I, M, U, V, X, partly T) lost points, because the notes leave timestamp regeneration unknown. All submissions resolve the signing conflict toward timestamp + '.' + raw body; Q and F lose fidelity for suggesting legacy parsed-JSON acceptance, and Q for labelling redirects as a guarantee. Could not run X (Flask unavailable offline). Y and K were run with a stub express module. Word counts come from OBJECTIVE_CHECKS; D is the only submission below 700.

It has 23 decisions and milestones with numbered acceptance criteria.

06-product-planning.notes: All 25 submissions delivered PLAN.md and RESPONSE.md; BRIEF/TASK files were unchanged. I read every plan and response in full and grepped for dates and staffing. Main differentiator: the 24h purge. Top plans make compliance hold by construction (A: a cap anchored to the server receipt time with an interlock; X/J/P: purge at server-confirmed submission; T: proactive purge after submission sync) or gate acceptance on purge (B/M/F, rigorous but heavy on the product). Mid and lower plans purge only after learning of acceptance, measure from the next sync (U, C, I), or wait the full 24h (W, V, R). Close calls: A vs X. Both are excellent; A edges ahead on the purge proof and stale-signature handling, X is tighter. J vs P: J has the more concrete protocol, P better re-sign handling; both take inspector-wins. N/M/Q tie at 8.75: N has the most actionable milestones but redefines acceptance; M has the strongest risk rigor but the heaviest product burden; Q has balanced judgment but a vague offline-deadline rule. E/R/H tie at 6.0 for different failures. W/V tie at 5.5; W has broader coverage despite fake weekly rollout dates. T's process note (chat UI, no tools) doesn't affect a prose task; T claims no run outputs. I couldn't verify any claims about real systems; scoring rests on internal consistency, coverage of the brief's constraints, and correctness of the engineering reasoning.

07-creative-writing.notes: All 25 STORY.md files fall within 800-1,100 words by wc (881-1,099; B at 1,099 and M/S/U at 1,096-1,098 are near the cap). Constraint deductions: S (message 'eleven years out', 5-sentence RESPONSE), R ('nine years, four months'), W (stamp reads 'Today'; no ten-year marker), V (weather opening, labelled joke), M (labelled joke), B (markdown heading in RESPONSE). Closest calls: Y vs H vs C. C's 'Set 20 fast' clock clue is the most ingenious and fair reversal and has the best joke, so it ranks first. Y ranks above H because salt drives its turn directly and the breathing callback is cleaner; H is the most original and restrained but uses salt sparingly and its turn may be missed. N is roughly equal on prose but more elliptical. B/G/L are tied at 8.75; B ranks first because salt mechanically drives its turn, despite the restored-words logic gap. 08-social-media.notes: Closest calls: E vs C vs J. All are brand-clean. E edges ahead on voice ('receipts attached') plus fully grounded replies. C is the cleanest on facts but plainer. J has the best humour but adds 'spent the longest on' and 'opens beside it'. R, V, S and D tie at 9.0: R has the strongest voice but an invented refund offer; V has no inventions but is less distinctive. Cross-cutting: the main separator was invention in replies (support emails, Help-menu paths, 'resumes where it left off', Japanese support, lab licensing deals), which the brief forbids. Inferring 'no training' from 'processing stays local' was treated as acceptable. Submissions that refused to answer the training question (F, O) were judged honest but unhelpful and cold. Counts: all Bluesky posts and Bluesky replies are under 280/300 chars. M's LinkedIn post (115-116 words) fails the 120-word minimum and its self-reported counts are false. G's Instagram caption is 79 words excluding hashtags (82 including), borderline. N's RESPONSE.md is 151 words with its title (148 body). E's Instagram is 81 words excluding hashtags. Counting method: whitespace tokens containing an alphanumeric char; Bluesky chars computed on the post joined across wrapped lines. Could not verify how any real word counter treats hashtags or em dashes; borderline cases got at most 0.25 off.

M has top-tier evidence discipline but its customer update is an internal log narrative. H was capped on diagnosis for omitting the required contributing-factors section. P's process note (chat, no tools) did not matter since no execution was needed. No servers or background processes were started.

11-frontend-operations.notes: Closest calls: B vs I (both 9.25). B ranks first for density and its arrow-key chart; I has marginally better a11y but an empty initial detail. X vs C (9.0) separated on desktop judgement; X's mobile table is its weak spot. Several submissions (D, Q, T, U) override the [hidden] attribute with CSS display rules, so empty or placeholder states show alongside content. Each was confirmed with a visibility probe. 404 console errors in OBJECTIVE_CHECKS are favicon requests and were not penalised. F (fetch-only) is blank when opened via file://; N, Q, V, W fetch with an inline fallback (they log a CORS error on file:// but render). Contrast counts come from a heuristic scan of non-SVG text against composited backgrounds and may misjudge text over images or gradients. Not verified: screen-reader output, and dark-mode toggles beyond confirming they exist.
